roe.text: Ugin, Sorin Markov and Nahiri decided to rid the Multiverse of the Eldrazi, but since they could not defeat them, they chose to imprison them on Zendikar instead.
Together they devised a network of hedrons and leylines, with Nahiri building it and Ugin inscribing the runes, while Sorin lured the Eldrazi in and Ugin bound them with colorless magic.
When the Titans arrived on Zendikar, the three planeswalkers fought them, then combined their magic at the Eye of Ugin to activate the network and seal the Titans in stone.

They locked the Eye with a spell that needs three planeswalker sparks and Ugin's breath, then disbanded; Sorin and Ugin left, promising to return if Nahiri signaled, and she stayed behind to guard the prison.

ktk.text: Ugin began on Tarkir as a spirit dragon who shaped its landscape, creatures and peoples, and whose wing beats birthed the dragonstorms.

Nicol Bolas tracked him there and fought him, gravely injuring him, mining his mind for what he knew of the Eldrazi, and leaving him to die; in the original timeline the storms then ceased and the clans hunted the dragons to extinction.
Sarkhan Vol traveled back through the Nexus of Fate and saved Ugin by encasing him in hedrons, which created the current timeline and made the dragon tempests stronger.
In that timeline Sorin Markov arrived searching for Ugin, and Sorin's Restoration woke him, after which Ugin told Sorin to find Nahiri.

frf.text: Ugin's magic had coalesced over the millennia into dragon tempests that birthed five broods, each led by a dominant dragon revered by a clan.

Sarkhan Vol followed his whispers across time to the sky above Tarkir, where Nicol Bolas and Ugin clashed and Ugin was mortally wounded; Bolas had corrupted Yasova Dragonclaw to help him, and Yasova's spell gripped Sarkhan.
Sarkhan realized the whispers were Ugin's own plea, then activated the hedron around the dying dragon, preserving him and rewriting history.
In the new Tarkir, the khans debated whether to open Ugin's cocoon, kill him, or kill the brood-lords, while Yasova confessed that she had helped a malevolent dragon spirit attack him.

dtk.text: Ugin fell to Tarkir after fighting Nicol Bolas, who turned the dragons against him through Yasova's spell and delivered the deathblow that broke his body.
Sarkhan Vol then gave him a hedron shard, which unfolded into a protective cocoon, and Ugin slept for hundreds of years inside it.
In 4559 AR Sorin Markov used blood magic to destroy the shard and free him, and Ugin explained that Bolas had attacked him with his own dragons.

Sorin told him the Eldrazi had escaped, and Ugin insisted that all three of the original planeswalkers must work together, agreeing to join Sorin at the Eye of Ugin; he also met Sarkhan and explained how Tarkir's history had changed.

bfz.text: Awake again, Ugin learned that the Eldrazi had awakened, and went to the Eye of Ugin to rebuild the hedron network.
There Jace Beleren met him, and Ugin revealed he knew Jace had been one of the three planeswalkers who opened the Eye, manipulated by Nicol Bolas.
Ugin told Jace that Ulamog could not be killed and that the Eldrazi should be imprisoned again, stressing that the titans do not dwell in physical space and that the Eldrazi had come as three.

Jace argued that Zendikar was somebody's home, but Ugin said he was there to save the Multiverse, not its people, and Jace left despite his warnings; Ugin later berated the Gatewatch for killing Ulamog and Kozilek.

bbd.text: Ugin hatched with his twin Nicol from the last egg-stone and crashed through the canopy, where he held Nicol back as hunters netted and killed a dragon named Merrevia Sal.
Nicol wanted revenge, but Ugin urged finding their siblings first, and the twins flew to the peak together, where Ugin stared at the sky and asked where they had come from.

In Ugin's own words, they spent years perfecting tandem hunting before finding their sibling Arcades Sabboth ruling a human settlement, where they lived as guests and Ugin befriended the holy elder Te Ju Ki, who showed him globes of light she called planes.
When Nicol announced he had found a better way to get revenge and flew off without farewell, Ugin left Te Ju Ki to follow him.

m19.text: Ugin flew alone back toward the birth mountain, then rejoined Nicol to find human settlements that had turned their sister into an ornament, where poisoned bolts wounded him.

Later Ugin realized Nicol had caused a murder by whispering into a chief's son's mind and meant to manipulate him too, feeling that his twin had never truly cared for him; he was then torn into the space between planes and landed on Tarkir.
After mastering planeswalking, he confronted Nicol atop the birth mountain, told him he was a planeswalker, and left in fury and grief when Nicol called him a liar and a coward.

Bolas later attacked him in the Meditation Realm, chasing him across Zendikar, Kephalai and Ravnica; Ugin accepted death so that Nicol would stop, and a dragon reborn from the waters resolved to protect the planes.

war.text: Ugin let Bolas fatally wound him on the Meditation Plane, shattering it and casting Bolas away, and was reborn as a Spirit Dragon in a body formed from the Realm's waters.
He conspired with Sarkhan Vol and allied with Niv-Mizzet to plan Bolas's defeat, speaking to Araithia and Liliana through the Spirit-Gem, and Liliana gave up the Chain Veil.
After Bolas was defeated, Ugin took his body to the Meditation Realm and had Jace conceal this with an illusion of the corpse disintegrating.
Bolas woke powerless and nameless, and Ugin declared himself his jailer, merging with the sealed Meditation Realm to watch him until his natural death.

jmp.text: Ugin told Jace that the Eldrazi can be imprisoned by hedrons, though Jace doubted it, asking how that had worked out last time.

cmr.text: Sorin Markov mocked Ugin as entombed, telling him the corpses of worlds would join him in the tomb.

j22.text: Ugin told Jace that hedrons could imprison the Eldrazi, and Jace remained skeptical after how it had gone last time.

tdm.text: Narset believed Ugin's departure from Tarkir had unleashed the stronger dragonstorms, since he had served as a metaphysical ballast, and she eventually learned the secrets he had left behind.
In the Meditation Realm, Narset and Elspeth found Ugin with a chained dragon, and Ugin explained that he had made the realm a prison for his brother until Bolas dies millennia from now.
When Narset asked for help against the dragonstorms, Ugin said he could not help; then Jace seized the gem between his horns, and the realm burned away as Bolas's fetters came undone.
Ugin escaped to Tarkir, where the wild dragons fled at his arrival and he defeated Sarkhan with ghostfire, though he admitted that Bolas was free.
